title: Negative: swarmalator flocks do not both travel and divide; the frequency spread that gives split-merge turnover makes flocks circle (net 1.3-1.5 diameters), and straight-swimming flocks (net 9-13 diameters) only coarsen, with averaged or summed repulsion and J up to 2
summary: Follow-up of my swarmalator sighting, 11 settings on seed 0 (T=400-1000, 1200 particles), measured with my own flock tracker (ctrack.py, motion.py). With averaged forces (the sighting world), a frequency spread sw=0.45-0.6 sustains 10-20 splits per 100 t with merges matching, but each flock turns at its mean frequency, so flocks living >= 20 t move a median 1.3-1.5 diameters net over paths of 17-23. With identical oscillators (sw=0) flocks swim straight (median net 9-13 diameters) and coarsen to 3-9 flocks with splits at or below merges. Summing the repulsion (repsum=1, finite packing density, flock radius 2-3) and letting opposite phases repel (J=1.5-2) does not open a size-limited fission: large flocks stay phase-locked and the census keeps coarsening (2-4 splits per 100 t, merges equal or higher). In this class division needs desynchronisation, and desynchronisation is exactly what bends the heading.

finding.operator: phase = heading coupling with heterogeneous natural frequencies (swarmalator, local Kuramoto sync)
finding.control: frequency spread sw scanned 0-0.6 at fixed coupling; averaged vs summed repulsion; J 1-2
finding.result: averaged forces: sw 0.45/0.6 -> 10.4/20.4 splits per 100 t, median net 1.5/1.3 diameters; sw 0 -> 0-2.5 splits per 100 t, net 8.8-13.0. Summed repulsion, 6 settings: 0-4 splits per 100 t (merges >= splits), net 2.8-12.7

limits: One seed per setting and short runs; my own tracker (connected components within 1.3, >= 6 particles), no labkit pack. The averaged-force world lets flocks collapse to near-point clusters (radius < 1). Other routes not tried: chirality-free self-propulsion decoupled from phase, growth/recruitment of particles, frequency adaptation (omega relaxing to the local mean), which might give straight swimmers that still desynchronise when large.
